items.title: Bomb found at ethanol plant in Illinois, forcing evacuations, officials say
items.brief: A bomb was found at an ethanol plant in central Illinois on Friday, officials said, sparking an investigation involving the FBI and forcing the evacuation of thousands of people living nearby.

items.title: This Minnesota mayoral race was a dead-even tie. So, they drew the winner’s name from a bag
items.brief: A four-vote lead is hardly a commanding margin, but the incumbent mayoral candidate in Spring Lake Park, Minnesota, appeared to have edged ahead as election night drew to a close.

items.title: Tanker ‘lost control’ and hit cruise ship in New Orleans, spurring massive evacuation, officials say
items.brief: Passengers of a river cruise boat in New Orleans had to be pulled from the Mississippi river on Friday, after a tanker collided with the paddlewheeler as it sat in dock, causing it to capsize.

items.title: Immigrant community becomes epicenter of grief after deadly Brooklyn building collapse
items.brief: Leonor Yupa dropped to her knees Thursday when a Spanish-language media reporter said her 22-year-old son was among eight people whose lives were claimed by the Brooklyn building collapse the day before.

items.title: Trump to meet with China’s Xi and Russia’s Putin at historic trilateral sit-down on nuclear non-proliferation
items.brief: President Donald Trump will meet jointly next week with China’s leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, the White House said Friday, a first-ever trilateral sit-down between the leaders of the three…

items.title: The US has had the tools to control measles for almost 65 years. Here’s how it’s come raging back
items.brief: The United States is experiencing its worst and deadliest year for measles since 1991, with 10 measles-associated deaths so far in 2026 – half of which were reported in the past two weeks.

items.title: After 26 years, the US has lost its measles elimination status
items.brief: Thanks to widespread vaccination, measles had been considered “eliminated” as a continually transmitting illness in the United States since 2000 – but not anymore.

items.title: Rubio says more work to do and downplays election losses amid speculation about political future
items.brief: Amid speculation about his political future , Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared that there is more work to be done as he downplayed Republicans’ losses in the midterm elections.
